svg.title: Fever decision chart: hyperthermia (normal set point) is told apart from fever; fever is screened for sepsis with qSOFA or SIRS; a stable patient is sorted into a localised infection, a fever with rash or alarm sign, or a fever with no focus (fever of unknown origin), each with clues, investigations in order and management

svg.text: A patient with FEVER: is it really fever, is the patient STABLE, and WHERE is the infection?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: safety first: hand hygiene + personal protective equipment · methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) flag → contact precautions

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: fever = oral/tympanic ≥ 37.2°C at 6 AM or ≥ 37.8°C any time · children 38°C (rectal, armpit)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: older adults: 37.8°C once, 37.2°C persistent or ≥ 1.1°C over baseline · 30–50% of the frail have NO fever: look for falls,

svg.text: Set point RAISED: FEVER · screen for SEPSIS first

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: adults: quick SOFA (qSOFA) · respiratory rate (RR) ≥ 22 · BP ≤ 100/60 · altered mentation

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: children: systemic inflammatory response (SIRS) · temperature, heart rate > 90, RR > 20, white count · 2 or more = HIGH RISK
